text:
alex: Heads-up — we need a short plan for the next "Slate" DP intake window. churn was higher than expected last quarter; want to discuss buckets, acceptance cadence, and a couple of mitigation tactics. who can take notes?
mira: I can take notes. quick ask: do we keep cohort-size target or switch to rolling intake?
alex: leaning rolling intake but with fixed weekly caps (helps ops + gives steady feedback). propose: 30 total over 6 weeks, ~5 new seats/week. allows staging.
sam: +1 to weekly caps. also suggest we create a 'warm interest' bucket for folks who sign up but don't accept immediately — 2-week hold, 1 reminder, then soft-offer to next bucket. that reduced churn in past pilots.
jordan: can we define buckets concretely? e.g., {"active": offers sent, "warm": accepted interest/no show yet, "waitlist": qualified but no slot, "drop": declined}. ops-bot: auto-assign tags on signup: active/warm/waitlist.
emily: we should also add an onboarding micro-check (15m) within 48h of acceptance — converts ~60% of warm -> active in my experience.
alex: good — main mitigation tactics: onboarding micro-check, rolling weekly caps, warm bucket reminders, and a small incentive (credit + quickstart session). anyone opposed?
mira: no objections. question: recruitment messaging — do we change offer language to set clearer expectations about time commitment? sample copy below:```Hey — thanks for applying to Redwood Slate pilot. We run weekly limited seats, expect ~30–45 minutes/week for the first 3 weeks, and a one-off 15m kickoff. We provide $200 credit and priority access to new features. Accept within 72h to secure your slot.```
sam: love the clarity. maybe shorten to "Accept within 72h to hold your seat" — less formal. also add a nudge workflow: day-2 Slack/email nudge, day-5 final reminder.
jordan: on measurement: success metrics for this intake should be: 1) acceptance rate >= 60% of offers, 2) retention through week-3 >= 75% of accepted, 3) feedback NPS (or qualitative score) >= 8/10 from active participants.
emily: can we add a prompt-set quality gate? at onboarding ask them to run a short prompt with their main use-case — capture baseline quality and surface glaring model-fit issues early.
alex: yes. ops: what's the routing for overflow/waitlist? sam: auto-invite waitlist folks to next week's slot until they move to warm or active. also allow manual swap for high-value partners.
mira: logistics: need a short playbook for SRE/Eng availability — callouts for when to escalate model regressions reported by partners. I'll draft SLO expectations and a contact runbook.
alex: timeline: finalize messaging + buckets by EOD Fri, template invites by Mon, first rolling-cap cohort starts Tue following. who volunteers to own the invite template + automations?
sam: I own automations (nudge cadence + waitlist rules).
emily: I'll own onboarding checklist + prompt-set gate.
jordan: I'll draft success-metrics dashboard and hooks for Console (per-route retention).
mira: I'll produce the playbook + contact runbook. alex: perfect. small TODO summary: 1) invite copy (mira+sam) 2) automations (sam) 3) onboarding micro-check flow + prompt-set (emily) 4) success dashboard (jordan) 5) SRE/eng runbook (mira).
ops-bot: Reminder created: "Slate intake plan review" on calendar Tue 09:30 — attendees: alex, mira, sam, emily, jordan.
alex: one more item — escalation policy: if >=2 partners report regression within 48h, auto-pause new offers and trigger canary on fallback model. jordan — can you add that to dashboard alerts?
jordan: yep — will add alert threshold and a one-click pause button tile in Console mock.
emily: final thought: let's keep communication channels clear — #pilot-feedback for raw reports, weekly summary in this thread, and a short 10m sync each Friday morning during the intake.
sam: noted. I will stub the automation rules in the repo and share the RFC link here when done.
mira: thanks team. I'll publish the playbook draft in Google Drive and drop the link in this thread. :thumbsup:
alex: thanks — good plan. see you all on Tue."
